subject: Medisync POC: success charter, evaluation choices, and next steps
thread:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Medisync POC: success charter, evaluation choices, and next steps

Elena — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the pilot kickoff.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary objective: surface clinically-relevant patient-summary suggestions for care coordinators (reduce time spent drafting notes).
- Key success metric: reduction of time-to-final-note by >= 35% for the cohort, and FTR (first-time-acceptance) >= 75% for generated suggestions.
- Data scope: de-identified visit notes + structured vitals for sample of ~3k encounters (initial shadow sample).
- Constraints: no PHI leaves Medisync VPC; Redwood Private expected to be deployed in your staging VPC.

Proposed POC approach (two tracks we recommend):
1) Online shadow (preferred for real-time behavior): run Redwood in shadow mode for 2 weeks against live traffic subset (3x concurrency windows) to measure latency, QA pipeline, and acceptance rates.
2) Offline batch evaluation: run a 1k-record offline set through the same model variants, graded by your SME rubric and our hybrid scorer.

I attached a draft POC charter and an evaluation rubric (see attachments). High-level timeline we suggest:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria + sign-off on data access and security checklist.
- Week 1: infra provisioning and model selection (we'll provide 2 quantized variants).
- Week 2: shadow run + parallel offline grading.
- Week 4: review results and decide on expansion / dedicated capacity.

Action items I propose (owner in parens):
- Approve success criteria and grading weights (Elena / Samir)
- Confirm data export window & sample (Elena / ProdEng)
- Provision staging VPC peering and KMS access (Marissa)
- Redwood to provision shadow endpoint + baseline runbook (Ben)

Are you comfortable with that split (shadow + offline) as the primary evaluation? If so, can you confirm the SME availability for grading (we recommend 3 SMEs for 1 week)?

Thanks — I can hop on a short call tomorrow if helpful.

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

- eval-rubric-v2.xlsx (grading weights + sample judgments)

Quick technical note from infra:
- Shadow run capacity: we recommend a 10% mirror sample of production traffic for the first run to keep costs predictable and to validate cold-start behaviors. For your traffic profile, expect median added latency on the mirror path of ~30–45ms (non-blocking path).
- Model variants: we'll provision two variants: m-latest-16q (faster, lower-cost) and m-accuracy-8q (higher quality). We'll include token-level cost estimates in the drive doc.
- Grading approach: strongly recommend we run the offline 1k sample first through both variants to generate a baseline score. Then run the shadow and compare live acceptance rates. That lets us correlate offline rubric grades with live FTR.

My ask: Rachel / Marissa, if you can confirm the mirror sample percentage and the S3 path we'll pull the offline dataset from, infra will start provisioning today.
